diagnostic_evidence.quote: To rule out spurious constant offsets in the constant \(c\), we assume \(\Sigma_{YY}\) is invertible.
Next, we show that except for a small class of highly symmetric distributions within \(\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\) (including Gaussians), the EnKU is the \emph{unique} exact affine conditioning map.

Further, we showed that within $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$, the EnKU is the unique affine  exact conditioning map up to small symmetry classes $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}, \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}},$ and $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ (Theorem \ref{thm:enkf_update_unique}).

issues.failure_explanation: The roadmap sentence (and the abstract and Discussion) claim that, outside the symmetry classes, the EnKU is the only exact affine map for any $\pi\in\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ at $y_\star$, attributing this to Theorem 2. The actual uniqueness statement is Corollary 1, which additionally requires $\Sigma_{YY}$ non-singular; Theorem 2 itself only gives spectral/structural constraints and contains no uniqueness conclusion. The rank hypothesis is essential, not cosmetic: take $n=m=1$, $\pi=\Law(Z,0)$ with $Z$ a centered exponential. Then $\pi\in\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ (constant kernel $\Law(Z)$, $O(x,y)=x$), $K=0$, and every map $\ell(x,y)=x+By$ is exact at $y_\star=0$, so the EnKU is not unique; yet $\pi$ lies in none of the symmetry classes ($\mathrm{Var}Z=1$ excludes $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}$; $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}}$ would force $vZ$ a.s. constant; $(v_1Z,v_2Z)$ is supported on a ray and $Z$ is asymmetric, excluding $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$).

failure_location.quote: In Theorem \ref{thm:enkf_update_unique} we answer the second question: excluding strongly symmetric distributions, given $\pi \in \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$, $y_\star \in \R^m$ the EnKU update $L^{\mathrm{EnKU}}_{\pi, y_\star}$ is the \emph{only} affine map  that is exact for $\pi$ at $y_\star$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the uniqueness prose with non-singular $\Sigma_{YY}$ (or 'after projecting out singular directions of $Y$') and attribute the uniqueness conclusion to Corollary \ref{cor:enkf_char} rather than Theorem \ref{thm:enkf_update_unique}.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract, introduction roadmap, and Discussion overstate the uniqueness characterization: as written it fails for observation-degenerate laws in $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ outside all symmetry classes. No labelled formal result is affected; Corollary 1 already carries the required hypothesis.
issues.title: Uniqueness prose omits the non-singular $\Sigma_{YY}$ hypothesis (and misattributes it to Theorem 2)
issues.why_classification: The formal result is correct and already contains the needed hypothesis; the defect is confined to summary prose. The repair is a local qualifier and a pointer fix; every formal claim, method, and the advertised generic scope survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we ask what the largest possible set of measures  $\mathrm{F}$ is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for.
Clearly $\pi$ is not in $\mathrm{F}$ for general $f$ and has the exact affine conditioning map $L_{y_\star}(x,y) = f(y_\star)y$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract frames $\mathrm{F}$ as the largest set 'any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for' and concludes near-optimality 'among affine transports'. Formally, $\mathrm{F}$ is the union of exact sets over weakly $y_\star$-dependent maps only, and the paper's own Section 3.2 constructs laws outside $\mathrm{F}$ (hence outside $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\cup\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$) that nevertheless admit exact fully $y_\star$-dependent affine maps, e.g. $\pi=\Law(f(Y)Z,Y)$ with $L_{y_\star}(x,y)=f(y_\star)y$, and the rotated-square example whose slope depends on $y^\star$. Under the abstract's literal reading (union over all affine conditioning maps of Definition 1), the identity $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}\cup\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$ and the near-optimality statement are false; both hold only within the weakly $y_\star$-dependent class.

failure_location.quote: Thus, among  affine transports, the EnKU is near-optimal for exact distributional conditioning beyond the Gaussian setting.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the 'weakly $y_\star$-dependent' qualifier in the abstract's description of $\mathrm{F}$ and in the concluding near-optimality sentence.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract advertises a maximality/optimality guarantee over all affine conditioning maps, materially broader than what Theorem \ref{thm:F_char} establishes; the paper's own counterexamples show the broader reading is false. The formal statements in the main text are unaffected.
issues.title: Abstract describes F and near-optimality over all affine transports, but the result covers only weakly $y_\star$-dependent maps
issues.why_classification: Theorem \ref{thm:F_char} and its proof are correct; only the abstract's scope language drops the defining restriction. The repair is a two-word qualifier in prose; no formal claim or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \hat C_a := \frac{1}{N-1}\hat X_a \left(I_N - \frac{1}{N}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top\right)\hat X_a^\top,\quad  C_a = \hat C_f - \hat C_fH^\top (H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma)^{-1}H\hat C_f.

issues.failure_explanation: With $Z:=\hat X_f^{(c)}$, $\hat C_f=\frac{1}{N-1}ZZ^\top$ and analysis anomalies $\hat X_a^{(c)}=Z\hat T$, the stated condition gives $\hat C_a=\frac{1}{N-1}Z\hat T\hat T^\top Z^\top=\hat C_f-(N-1)\hat C_fH^\top S^{-1}H\hat C_f$ ($S:=H\hat C_fH^\top+\Gamma$), contradicting the required $C_a=\hat C_f-\hat C_fH^\top S^{-1}H\hat C_f$ by a factor $N-1$ in the correction term. The consistent condition is $\hat T\hat T^\top=I_N-\frac{1}{N-1}Z^\top H^\top S^{-1}HZ$ (equivalently $(I_N+\frac{1}{N-1}Z^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1}HZ)^{-1}$). Worse, the printed right-hand side need not be positive semidefinite: its nonzero eigenvalues include $1-(N-1)\mu$ with $\mu$ the eigenvalues of $S^{-1/2}(S-\Gamma)S^{-1/2}\in[0,1]$, so for small $\Gamma$ and $N>2$ it is indefinite and the principal square root the paper then defines does not exist.

failure_location.quote: \hat T \hat T ^\top  =  I_N - \left(\hat X_f^{(c)}\right)^\top H^\top\left(H\hat C_fH^\top + \Gamma\right)^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the subtracted term by $\frac{1}{N-1}$, i.e. $\hat T\hat T^\top=I_N-\frac{1}{N-1}(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top(H\hat C_fH^\top+\Gamma)^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)}$ (equivalently use the standard Woodbury form $(I_N+\frac{1}{N-1}(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1}H\hat X_f^{(c)})^{-1}$).
issues.overall_effect: The ETKF as specified in the appendix fails its stated Gaussian-consistent moment guarantee, and the transform $\hat T$ as constructed is generally undefined. Downstream content survives: the generalized transform $\hat T'$ the paper subsequently uses is exactly the scale-invariant projector form that the corrected condition also yields, and the conclusion that the generalized ETKF coincides with the EnKU (verified by direct computation in the source) is unaffected.
issues.title: ETKF transform condition misses the $1/(N-1)$ factor; stated $\hat T\hat T^\top$ is inconsistent with the moment conditions and generally not PSD
issues.why_classification: A single forced normalization fix makes the display consistent with the paper's own moment conditions, and no substantive claim is lost: the generalized transform and the ETKF=EnKU equivalence hold identically, and no main result depends on the erroneous display.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\hat A\in \R^{n\times n}$ is therefore a matrix satisfying
$$
\hat A \hat C_f\hat A^\top = \hat C_a.
$$

where $\hat X_f^{(c)} = F G U^T$ is the SVD  and $(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1} H\hat X_f^{(c)}= C D C^T$  is the eigenvalue decomposition  with the eigenvectors in the null space  arranged as the final columns of \(C\).

issues.failure_explanation: The formula $\hat A^{(3)}=ZC(I+D)^{-1/2}G^\dagger F^\top$ (with $Z:=\hat X_f^{(c)}$, $Z=FGU^\top$, $Z^\top H^\top\Gamma^{-1}HZ=CDC^\top$) fails the moment condition it is introduced to satisfy. From the paper's own definitions: take $n=m=2$, $N=3$, $H=\Gamma=I_2$, and the centered anomaly matrix $Z=\begin{pmatrix}3&-3&0\\1&1&-2\end{pmatrix}$. Then $\hat C_f=\mathrm{diag}(9,3)$, $\hat C_a=\mathrm{diag}(0.9,0.75)$, $D=\mathrm{diag}(18,6,0)$, and the formula gives $\hat A^{(3)}=\mathrm{diag}(1/\sqrt{19},1/\sqrt7)$, hence $\hat A^{(3)}\hat C_f\hat A^{(3)\top}=\mathrm{diag}(9/19,3/7)\neq\hat C_a$. Relative to the standard EAKF SVD form $ZC(I+\tfrac{1}{N-1}D)^{-1/2}C^\top Z^\dagger$ (which does satisfy the condition), the display has two defects: the eigenvalue shift is not rescaled by $\frac{1}{N-1}$, and the factor $C^\top U$ is missing (it should be $C^\top Z^\dagger=C^\top UG^\dagger F^\top$, not $G^\dagger F^\top$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula with a correct EAKF transform, e.g. $\hat X_f^{(c)}C(I+\tfrac{1}{N-1}D)^{-1/2}C^\top UG^\dagger F^\top$ (equivalently $\hat X_f^{(c)}C(I+\tfrac{1}{N-1}D)^{-1/2}C^\top(\hat X_f^{(c)})^\dagger$), or delete the unused sentence.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed 'practically preferred' EAKF choice is mathematically invalid as written. The error is contained: $\hat A^{(3)}$ is never used again — only $\hat A^{(1)}$ and $\hat A^{(2)}$ (both correct) are identified with the compared methods $L^{\mathrm{OT}}$ and $L^{\mathrm D}$.
issues.title: Stated EAKF transform $\hat A^{(3)}$ does not satisfy its defining equation $\hat A\hat C_f\hat A^\top=\hat C_a$
issues.why_classification: The display is demonstrably false, but it sits in expository background and has no dependents; replacing it with the correct expression or deleting it fully repairs the paper with no loss to any substantive claim.
